cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4 absorbs T3's combination idea as a variable; T5 answers T4's protocol with its cost.
cells.limitation: T6 and T9 largely ignore preceding turns; Holistic Observer runs parallel to the others.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T3 adds combination hypothesis; T6 adds order and time of day of application.
cells.limitation: T7 restates T1/T4 isolation; T6's order-of-application point is never used later.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T5 and T8 set the cost of testing against the value of knowing the culprit.
cells.limitation: Whether one-by-one reintroduction can detect a combination effect (T3) is never examined.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T9 merges T2's stop with T1's reintroduction one at a time.
cells.limitation: T9 declares agreement while the isolation-versus-not-testing dispute of T7/T8 stays unresolved.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section E branches by severity and determination to keep the products.
cells.limitation: Ending repeats T1/T2's stop-then-reintroduce; how to identify the culprit is no sharper.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T4 takes T3's combination hypothesis seriously and folds it into the method.
cells.limitation: T5 recasts the user's wish to find the cause as mere scientific curiosity.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T8 tests T7: if all products sting, testing buys pain for a dispensable data point.
cells.limitation: T7 answers T6 with a slogan; T8's objection gets no reply from the Reductionist.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T3's opening aphorism matches Hippocrates' first aphorism; Bacon and Taleb stances fit their works.
cells.limitation: T2's 'permanent damage' overstates stinging risk; Section D credits T9 with an unargued point.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T3 flags the combination idea as a 'perhaps' rather than a fact.
cells.limitation: T7 'you will never know' and T5 'only priority' state contestable views as certainties.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T2 explicitly agrees with stopping while rejecting the experimental rationale.
cells.limitation: No speaker concedes or revises; Reductionist never answers T5/T8 cost objections.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A names the pull between identifying the irritant and protecting the skin now.
cells.limitation: Never asks whether the user wants to keep the products or just end the stinging.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T1 uses the three-products fact to propose stopping all and reintroducing singly.
cells.limitation: Product types, actives and timing of onset never inform the argument.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Section E keeps a branch for a user determined to use the products.
cells.limitation: T5 and T8 override the stated goal of finding the cause with abandoning products.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T5 names the ongoing cost of stinging during any testing period.
cells.limitation: No mention of allergic warning signs or when stinging warrants prompt medical care.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on severe versus mild stinging and unknown baseline.
cells.limitation: Never asks which products, ingredients, or other symptoms; the decisive facts go unbranched.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: Section E distinguishes a user determined to keep products from one who is not.
cells.limitation: No alternative motives offered as questions; T5 implies curiosity without asking.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T8 questions whether the user needs all these products; T3 questions single-culprit assumption.
cells.limitation: Neither assumption is put to the user as something to check.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T5 sets comfort against knowledge as competing priorities.
cells.limitation: The conflict is asserted by Taleb, never framed as the user's choice to weigh.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T2 touches fear of permanent damage.
cells.limitation: No attention to sunk cost, appearance worries, or advice pressures behind adopting three products.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section E offers branches the user can place themselves in.
cells.limitation: Turns are mostly imperatives ('must', 'Cease'); few distinctions offered to accept or refine.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Options span stop all, reintroduce singly, drop products, consult a professional.
cells.limitation: No limited step such as a patch test or checking labels for shared actives.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T8 prices testing in extra pain against a dispensable data point.
cells.limitation: Cost of stopping everything (lost benefits, slow multi-week trial) never stated.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: severe or persistent stinging favours stopping; mild favours staged reintroduction.
cells.limitation: No observable thresholds; 'baseline' and 'multi-day buffer' left undefined.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: T3 raises single product versus combination as the open unknown.
cells.limitation: Irritant versus allergic reaction, the consequential unknown, is never separated.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: Stop, let skin settle, reintroduce one at a time (T1, T9, Section E).
cells.limitation: Omits checking ingredient lists and red-flag medical care; professional only if baseline unclear.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T1 and T8 give plain, direct instructions and reasoning.
cells.limitation: T3 and T6 drift into abstraction: 'natural equilibrium', 'changing landscape'.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T5 'Your protocol' clearly points to T4.
cells.limitation: T9 'We are in agreement' leaves unclear who agrees with whom and on what.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Nine turns, all within range, each a single point.
cells.limitation: Strict A-B-C rotation with similar lengths gives a monotonous cadence.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Isolation (Bacon), subtraction (Taleb), and system view (Hippocrates) stay distinct.
cells.limitation: No speaker ever marks a change of position.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Section E condenses the debate into three branches.
cells.limitation: T4 and T7 repeat the isolation claim; T5 and T8 repeat stop everything.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T5 and T8 pit further skin harm against the wish to know.
cells.limitation: Tension is low: all agree on stopping from T2 onward.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T2 agrees with T1's action while rejecting its rationale.
cells.limitation: No reversal; T9's agreement names no argument that changed anyone's mind.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T2 'just survive the day' gives Taleb a blunt edge.
cells.limitation: Hippocrates speaks in generic gentleness; Bacon's turns are interchangeable.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T7 'Observation without isolation is just a narrative we tell ourselves.'
cells.limitation: No concrete skincare example or analogy anchors any turn.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T8 raises the 'all sting' scenario as a late twist.
cells.limitation: Flat rhythm; positions rotate without building toward a turn or climax.

strengths: Section E gives conditional branches by severity and by determination to keep the products.
T8 offers a real objection to T7's protocol: testing may buy pain for a dispensable answer.
Three minds hold clearly distinct stances (isolation, subtraction, system view) throughout T1-T9.
weaknesses: The debate never asks which products or actives are involved, the facts that most decide the culprit.
No red-flag guidance on allergic signs or when stinging needs prompt medical care (Section E, all turns).
T9 declares agreement without any concession; the Reductionist never answers T5/T8 cost objections.

symptoms.observed: Never asks which products, ingredients or extra symptoms; method stays generic.
symptoms.evidence: Cease all three products immediately until the skin returns to baseline

symptoms.observed: Section E gives no warning signs or route to prompt medical care.
symptoms.evidence: If the stinging is severe or persistent stop all products

symptoms.observed: Reductionist repeats isolation and never answers the cost-of-testing objection.
symptoms.evidence: Unless you test each product individually, you will never know

symptoms.observed: Agreement declared while T7/T8 dispute over testing stays open.
symptoms.evidence: We are in agreement on the reset. Let the skin heal first.

symptoms.observed: Section E conditions lack observable thresholds; buffer and baseline undefined.
symptoms.evidence: introduce only one product at a time with a multi-day buffer

findings.description: No allergic warning signs (swelling, hives, blistering, eye involvement) or advice on when to seek prompt medical care; professional consult offered only for unclear baseline.
Risk of 'permanent damage' from new-product stinging is overstated as the rationale for stopping.
Credits the Holistic Observer with arguing the skin is an unreliable testing ground; no turn argues this beyond T9's 'let the skin heal first'.
Claim that the body rejects what it does not recognize is not characteristic of the Aphorisms; attribution unverified.

rubric_fit_notes: A practical skin-irritation troubleshooting question gives criterion 4 little natural material; low C4 ratings reflect missed openings (sunk cost, wanting to keep products) rather than mismatch. Safety omission weighed in C3.4 and C5.5.
question_type_note: Read as a decision (troubleshooting) question: options were stopping, staged reintroduction, dropping products or seeking professional help, judged on observable conditions.
